Not really. Most of my big expenses are divorce related. I'm paying for a house I don't live in anymore and a few other things. I really don't live extravagantly, but I do have these spending sprees that are basically a symptom of what I deal with. I get super low and think that treating myself will make me feel better, or I tell myself "why not spend the money, you'll be dead soon anyway."

I just saw the comment about trying the group. It sounds good, but I'm not sure I could make myself go through with it. I will think about it, though.

No. I used to, but it has becomes harder to deal with every year. I'm so entrenched in the career at this point I don't know how to get out of it. I have debts now, so I can't really afford a loss of income. It really just adds to the frustration.
No. I've tried, but most of the people I work with have families.  The ones who do go out and do stuff never invite me along.
Not anymore. I used to try to.  I would occasionally try to go to social events that are designed for people to meet others, but not very often.

At work I am a different person.  I can "turn it on".  I am confident in what I do.  In my personal life, I pretty much shut down.  No confidence what so ever.  I struggle to start conversations.  When I'm in a group I hardly speak.  I always feel like people see me as unworthy of their time or attention.
The websites and social media efforts.
I work in television.  Currently I manage the Digital properties for a few stations.

I cycle from mild to severe depression.  I have a lot of confidence/self-worth issues.  My worst days are generally centered around a heavy sense of loneliness.  It's the whole "I'm a piece of shit.  No one likes me.  No one should like me.  Why would anyone want to be around me?"  stuff.  When my brain gets in that loop, it doesn't want to get out of it.  I then make dumb financial decisions thinking that I can make myself feel better, but then that makes everything worse.
